title: Dossier Base Schema
description: Base schema defining the canonical structure of a Dossier ACDC. A schema S IS-A dossier iff S's top-level allOf array contains a $ref to this schema's SAID, or recursively to another schema that IS-A dossier. A dossier SHOULD NOT include an issuee; all evidence MUST be carried in e, never in a.

s.description: SAID of the schema applied to this dossier.

r.description: Optional ACDC rules block. Compact form: SAID string. Expanded form: object.

a.description: Proximate metadata block. Compact form: SAID string. Expanded form: object with metadata about the dossier itself. MUST NOT carry primary evidence.

assembly_dt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp recording when the dossier was assembled. Distinct from the envelope issuance date, which may differ if the dossier was finalized and anchored later.

assembler.description: AID or human-readable name of the entity that curated the evidence collection. Useful when the assembler differs from the issuer.

purpose.description: Brief human-readable statement of why the dossier was assembled and what decisions it supports. Not intended for machine interpretation.

ref.description: External reference identifier (case number, docket number, transaction ID) linking the dossier to a record in an external system. Intentionally untyped; meaning is governance-context-determined.

gov.description: SAID or URI of the governance framework, policy document, or rulebook under which the dossier was assembled.

evt_dt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the event the dossier documents (e.g., the time of a crash, crime, filing, or transaction). Distinct from assembly_dt, which records when the evidence was curated.

evt_loc.description: Description of where the documented event or subject matter occurred. No single format is mandated; precision varies by domain. Implementers SHOULD follow domain standards (e.g., ISO 6709 for geographic coordinates).

jur.description: Legal or regulatory jurisdiction within which the dossier's subject matter falls, or under whose authority the evidence was collected. This identifies a legal/regulatory jurisdiction, not a geographic location. Expressed as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, optionally extended with an ISO 3166-2 region code (e.g., 'US-TX', 'FR', 'CA-ON'). MAY be an array when multiple jurisdictions apply.

cls.description: Domain-dependent classification of the matter the dossier documents. Examples: a statute reference or offense code (law enforcement); an event type code (NTSB); a case type such as 'civil', 'criminal', or 'appellate' (court). SHOULD reference a controlled vocabulary; MAY be a URI identifying a vocabulary entry.

phase.description: Procedural maturity of the dossier at issuance, e.g., 'preliminary', 'factual', 'final' (NTSB); 'investigation', 'adjudication', 'closed' (law enforcement). Distinct from revocation or annotation state of individual edges. When phase transitions, a new dossier version SHOULD be issued.

gov_rules.description: SAID or URI of the specific protocol, standard, or ruleset that governed the collection of evidence (e.g., a forensic collection protocol, the Federal Rules of Evidence, or NTSB investigation procedures). More specific than gov: gov names the framework overseeing the dossier; gov_rules names the procedural constraints on the underlying investigation.

fi.description: Finalization identifier. Optional AID used in joint issuance. When present and non-null, it tells a verifier to expect a finalization event for this dossier's joint issuance in the KEL of the named AID, which collects threshold-satisfying proofs in one place. When absent or null, no finalization event is promised and a verifier must gather endorsements from the participants' individual KELs.

attest.description: Declaration the issuer makes in their own voice about the collection, as part of the act of issuing it. The anchor establishes that the issuer issued the dossier; confirmed establishes whether the issuer adopted the declaration it carries, so a required declaration can be present and recorded as withheld.

statement.description: Human-readable text of the declaration. Where the declaration has legal effect, its wording usually comes from the governing framework named by gov or gov_rules.

confirmed.description: Whether the issuer affirms the statement.

manifest.description: Enumeration of the components the dossier is expected to contain, keyed by an identifier drawn from the governing framework, including components with no corresponding edge. Lets a dossier attest to its own negative space: an omission becomes an attributable claim rather than an inference from silence.

status.description: Disposition of this component. Defined values: provided (present, with edge naming the edge that carries it); pending (required and to follow, with due); not_applicable (not required of this issuer in this instance, with reason); withheld (required, not supplied, not promised, with reason). Implementers may define others appropriate to their framework.

reason.description: Grounds for a status of not_applicable or withheld.

due.description: ISO 8601 date by which a pending component is expected.

edge.description: Name of the edge in e that carries this component's evidence. Required when status is provided, and must name an edge present in the dossier. This is a pointer into the evidence graph, not evidence: a verifier that ignores the manifest still recovers the full graph from e.

e.description: Edges block linking to evidence. Compact form: SAID string. Expanded form: object whose additional properties each describe one edge. Specific edge shapes (n/s pairs for ACDC-native evidence; MxN/RMxN/MxQ/RMxQ operator groups for joint issuance) are defined by derived schemas.
